reason: Phyllary and leaf-tooth tips that end in a small, stiff, spine-like bristle; spine-tipped (ending in a spine) covers this. If curators want the awn too, add awn PO_0025349 present (rule for 'aristate').
'sub-' + saccate: the value saccate FLOPO:0991140 with value_qualifier approximately and 'sub' as cue.
Uncompressed fruits are not flattened. PATO's 'compressed' is only a synonym of condensed, which is a different sense, so the negation must be of flattened.

Mixes two things: cells lined up in vertical rows on a bulb coat, and cyme branches arranged one above another. PATO vertical (PATO_0001854) is the orientation of the bearer itself and fits neither safely.

'Widely ovate' = broadly ovate. The shape is ovate; the extra width is a length-to-width ratio (docs/odp/11) when the flora gives it. If a 'broadly ovate' class is ever added, this word becomes its synonym.
States that stellate hairs are missing, i.e. no part that is a star-shaped trichome. PO has no stellate trichome class, so the part is trichome plus PATO stellate (an exact synonym of star shaped).
Same reading as the earlier rule C172 for 'narrowed'. 'Base' goes to the region slot (plant organ base FLOPO_0985024, or leaf lamina base PO_0008019 on a blade).
The second number of 'blade 2-3 × 2-3 mm' is a width measurement. The blade is the bearer (lamina PO_0025060, or leaf lamina PO_0020039 on leaves), so no new term is needed.
Blade-bearing bracts or leaves have a lamina, as opposed to bladeless sheaths or scales.
Same reading as the earlier rule C181 for 'expanded'. 'Broadly' says how much, which no term records.
A piece of the part name 'brood leaves' (leaves bearing propagules), not a quality. Neither PO nor FLOPO has a class for it.
Bulblet is a synonym of PO bulb, which fits bulblets at the plant base. Bulblets in leaf axils are bulbils, i.e. aerial tuber PO_0004548.

reason: Two hair qualities joined: grey-hairy (canescent FLOPO:0991079) and finely hirsute (hirsutulous: no term; nearest is hirsute FLOPO:0991050 with a degree qualifier). Both are true at once, so this is not a range between two values like 'linear-lanceolate'.
Chalk white is a flat, opaque white. The colour is white.
Clavulate is the diminutive of clavate: slightly club-shaped. 'Clavulate-obtuse' hair tips and spurs fit PATO clavate.
A network of ridges on fruit sides and of exine walls on pollen. The FLOPO reticulate definition names both. 'Coarsely' says how coarse, which no term records.
Says the colour was not recorded. That is a gap in the data, not a quality of the plant.
A colour comparison without the part it is compared with, like 'darker' (earlier rejection C242).

label: fugacious
definition: A shedability quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's withering or falling away very soon after it has formed. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991181 marcescent (withering but staying on) and PATO:0001731 deciduous (plant). Caducous (falling early, without withering first) is kept apart.
reason: A standard botanical lifespan term with no PATO or FLOPO term. 'Early-withering' bracts and basal leaves are fugacious.
PATO plumose has the exact synonym 'feathery' and fits featherlike bracts. 'Featherlike venation pattern' is a vein colour pattern on petals and leaves and should not take this rule.
Vague: a 'very full' coma or inflorescence and 'glands full' do not name one quality.
A shape between two values, oblong and linear, written as one hyphenated word, like 'linear-lanceolate'. 'Narrowly' leans toward linear.
Negates PATO cleft: the calyx tube or staminal appendage is not split.
Negates PATO slender (narrow for its length) on pedicels and peduncles.
Spinose = spiny. 'Not becoming spinose' on buds adds a stage (when mature), which goes to the stage context.
